scope: Measurements only; production source and installations unchanged.

method.build: Release, current source snapshot with diagnostic instrumentation; Android trimming and AOT disabled as shipped
method.startup: First install measured separately. Five fresh-process repeats with an existing empty database, then five with ten saved 20-entry armies. Windows opens Home; Android restores its roster on the saved-army runs. OS file caches are not reset.
method.operations: Windows: 20 recorded samples per case. Android: 5 recorded samples per case in fresh-process batches after the long stress run aborted in Mono. One unrecorded warm-up per case. Each sample resets the fixture outside the timer. Ten saved armies. Commands use the shared session; native WPF/MAUI presentation follows. No touch-input injection.
method.readiness: Two rendering callbacks after presentation. These are render-readiness proxies, not hardware display/input latency measurements.
method.percentiles: Nearest-rank p95. Windows has 20 interaction samples per case; Android has 5, so its p95 equals the observed maximum and must not be treated as a reliable tail estimate. Startup has 5 samples per state.
method.memory: Managed heap without forced GC; allocated bytes are cumulative allocation, not resident memory. Windows uses precise allocation sampling; Android interaction batches use approximate counters after runtime thread-suspension assertions in the long run. Windows working set and Android PSS are different OS metrics.
limitations: Synthetic Death Guard fixtures, not the user database.
Android receives its bundled Stratagem supplement; Windows uses its own normal bundled library. Library card counts differ, so ratios are not pure hardware comparisons.
Diagnostic timings include instrumentation overhead; its exact cost was not isolated.
Desktop command work runs through the shared async harness before native rendering; this does not measure production UI-thread blocking or input latency.
UI.RenderSubmit includes presentation calculations, control creation, and binding work; it is not a GPU-only or layout-only measurement.
The initial Windows datasheet case incorrectly called full Render; its 40 samples were excluded and replaced by 40 samples using the actual RefreshDetails path. Both raw runs are retained.
Background applications and OS caches were not reset.
No scrolling gesture/frame-jank benchmark: phone input injection is restricted.
No optimizations applied; there is no before/after speedup claim.

validation.android_release_build: Passed; final APK passed native startup-binding check for ARM64 and x64 and completed physical-device batches
validation.cleanup: Temporary com.grimlist.perfpass package removed after collection; production com.grimlist.mobile remained at version 0.2.6/code 8 with unchanged update timestamp.
validation.android_collector: The long Android run did not produce valid interaction data. Crash logs show two native Mono thread-suspension assertions. It was replaced by short checkpointed batches, with approximate allocation counters and process-exit detection. The runtime assertion cause is unconfirmed.

ranked_recommendations.target: Phone datasheet and rules display preparation
ranked_recommendations.evidence: 20-unit datasheet: 5.62 s overall, including 4.45 s preparing data; enhancement preparation 3.21 s; attachment preparation 3.70 s.
ranked_recommendations.recommendation: Profile the individual PrepareUnit steps, reuse effective unit/rule results throughout one refresh, and consider calculating attachment/enhancement choices on demand. Invalidate affected results when equipment, rules, attachments or the library change.

ranked_recommendations.target: Windows screen refresh and repeated presentation calculations
ranked_recommendations.evidence: 20-unit equipment: 1.56 s overall versus 0.19 s command; Render submit 1.17 s. Attachments: 2.70 s overall, Render submit 2.05 s.
ranked_recommendations.recommendation: Split Render/RefreshDetails by changed region; reuse unchanged controls and derived display values. Render submit includes calculations as well as constructing controls, so profile its substeps before attributing all cost to layout.

ranked_recommendations.target: Library startup and memory footprint on both platforms
ranked_recommendations.evidence: Empty Home startup 3.54 s Windows / 7.84 s phone. Phone load/normalization 3.21 s, projection recovery 1.26 s, dataset indexes 2.07 s; 726 MiB cumulative managed allocations.
ranked_recommendations.recommendation: Reduce data materialized before readiness; evaluate lazy faction/datasheet loading and persisted reusable indexes. This is a larger storage/indexing change requiring correctness checks.

ranked_recommendations.evidence: Returning home with ten 20-unit armies costs 0.80 s; Windows HomeView recalculates every army, while Android already uses cached summaries.
ranked_recommendations.recommendation: Use the existing shared cached army summaries on Windows, then update only changed cards.

ranked_recommendations.evidence: Phone 20-unit equipment command 0.62 s and attachment command 1.45 s; direct saves roughly 5–6 ms and copies roughly 1–3 ms.
ranked_recommendations.recommendation: Measure normalization and eligibility/validation substeps next. Defer broad SQL-save and clone rewrites: these measured costs do not justify putting them first.

measurement_notes.android_native_crash: mono_threads_suspend_begin_async_resume assertion; two occurrences in the initial long-run diagnostic package. Production reproduction and root cause were not established.
measurement_notes.startup_builds: Empty-home startup was collected before changing the diagnostic allocation sampler; saved-army startup was collected from the revised diagnostic build. Production performance logic was unchanged.
measurement_notes.android_thermal: Thermal service status 0 before and after; battery temperature 31.0 C before and 33.6 C after.
